_comment: Every cell here cites the evidence file it is drawn from. This file is the single source scripts/05_generate_capability_chart.py reads; the chart is never hand-drawn from numbers typed directly into plotting code.

statuses.workaround: Expressed, but only via a workaround outside the plain rule
statuses.wrong: Silently produced a DIFFERENT result, not merely absent
statuses.impossible: Cannot be expressed in this engine at all

capability_labels.volumetric_threshold: N ticket requests per principal in T minutes
capability_labels.absence_of_event: Absence of a qualifying event for one principal
capability_labels.silent_wrong_result: Worst silent-wrong result found in this project

stateless_field_match.note: Base rule compiles to a plain row-returning SELECT.

volumetric_threshold.note: Requires a SEPARATE correlation rule type layered on the base rule by id reference; compiles to a GROUP BY/HAVING aggregate, not row-returning events.

field_typed_comparison.note: Every condition is a typed field comparison by construction.

absence_of_event.note: condition:{lt:1} compiles without error but the compiled SQL (GROUP BY ... HAVING event_count < 1) can never match, since GROUP BY never emits a row for an empty group. Reasoned from the rule model and demonstrated live; no SigmaHQ primary source states this limitation explicitly (see FINDINGS.md).

silent_wrong_result.note: pySigma is a compiler, not an evaluator: it cannot itself produce a wrong RESULT because it never runs a query against data. Its risk surface is a wrong COMPILATION (see the splunk_windows source-field mismatch under SPL), not a wrong evaluation.

stateless_field_match.note: Correctly evaluates the base rule; 0 hits on the volumetric corpus because that corpus's real TicketOptions value never matches the base rule's filter (a corpus fact, not a Zircolite defect).

volumetric_threshold.note: Correctly evaluates the pySigma-compiled correlation SQL end to end (proven with a synthetic 12-event fixture) and returns an aggregate row, but silently folds the base rule into the correlation and loads it as ONE rule ("Converted 1 rules"), not two.

field_typed_comparison.note: SQLite-backed, so every comparison is a typed column comparison.

absence_of_event.note: Inherits the same unsatisfiable compiled SQL from pySigma; Zircolite executes exactly what it is given and that query can never match.

silent_wrong_result.note: Native -x/--xml-input mode silently processes only 1 of 159 real events in the corpus's actual multi-root XML file format (170.3 KB file, reports "Total events processed: 1 (0 filtered out)"), a clean, confident, zero-error success that is completely wrong for the volumetric question the file exists to answer.

stateless_field_match.note: Reference published detection is a plain per-event search. NOT run against live Splunk in this project (auth unavailable).

volumetric_threshold.note: SPL's own `stats`/`eventstats` pipeline expresses this directly in one search (the published reference detection uses a 3-sigma anomaly calculation, richer than a flat threshold), unlike Sigma which needs a second rule TYPE. Not executed live.

absence_of_event.note: stats can enumerate a wider universe of principals and filter to count=0, expressing absence directly, something the compiled Sigma correlation structurally cannot do. Not executed live (Splunk auth unavailable).

silent_wrong_result.note: pySigma's splunk_windows pipeline hardcodes source="WinEventLog:Security" only; this corpus's own published test fixture declares source=XmlWinEventLog:Security for this exact data, and the hand-authored reference query's macro ORs both conventions. A query built with the pySigma pipeline would return zero matches on this corpus's own documented ingestion convention, looking exactly like a true negative. Confirmed from pipeline source code and the corpus's own metadata, NOT from a live search (Splunk auth unavailable).

stateless_field_match.note: Matches on flattened text substrings only; correctly fires on the true-positive event using multiple co-occurring substrings as a proxy for a field match.

volumetric_threshold.note: No event stream, no grouping, no time window concept at all.

field_typed_comparison.note: Cannot bind a string match to a named field. Demonstrated false positive: an unrelated EventCode=4688 process-creation event (Splunk Universal Forwarder's own splunk-netmon.exe, New Process ID 0x177c) is flagged because the substring 0x17 occurs inside an unrelated field's value.

absence_of_event.note: YARA only reports matches; it has no query language construct for "the count of matches is zero," and a scan with zero hits is indistinguishable from a scan that never ran.

silent_wrong_result.note: The substring-only rule matched a real, unrelated EventCode=4688 process-creation event (Splunk Universal Forwarder's own splunk-netmon.exe) as if it were a kerberoasting event, because "New Process ID: 0x177c" contains the literal text "0x17". This is not an absence of a result; it is a positive match on the wrong thing, indistinguishable in the tool's own output from a genuine hit.
